target.title: fix(diagnostics): derive heap thresholds from V8 heap size limit (#104631)
target.body:
Closes #104631

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users running the gateway with `NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size` above the default (e.g. 8 GB on a 15 GB RAM host) receive false-positive `heap_threshold` critical memory pressure diagnostics as soon as `heapUsedBytes` reaches 2 GB, even when the V8 heap limit has 75%+ headroom and the system has abundant free memory.

This triggers unnecessary diagnostic events, log noise, and stability bundle writes, and can cause downstream monitoring or supervisor restart chains (the linked issue reports a gateway drain-and-restart sequence on the reporter's setup).

## Why This Change Was Made

The diagnostic memory classifier previously hardcoded heap pressure thresholds at 1 GiB (warning) and 2 GiB (critical) — values that were reasonable for Node's default `--max-old-space-size` (~2 GB server / ~4 GB desktop) but do not scale when operators configure a larger heap limit.

This change derives default heap warning and critical thresholds from V8's effective `heap_size_limit`, so they automatically adapt to whatever `--max-old-space-size` is set:

- **Critical**: 75% of the V8 heap limit, floored at 2 GiB
- **Warning**: 60% of the V8 heap limit, floored at 1 GiB

The conservative lower bounds ensure small-heap or default-heap environments remain equally protected. RSS threshold and RSS growth detection are unchanged. No configuration key is added — the fix is fully automatic.

## User Impact

Users on decently-provisioned hosts (e.g. `--max-old-space-size=8192`) no longer see spurious `heap_threshold` critical pressure from routine heap usage at 2 GB, while the same protection level is preserved for default or constrained heap sizes. The change is invisible to operators: no new config, no migration, no restart requirement beyond the usual update.

## Evidence

### Unit tests

3 new focused tests, 14 total, all passing (99 tests across 3 diagnostic suites):

| Test | What it proves |
|------|---------------|
| `default heap thresholds never go below the original constants as a conservative lower bound (#104631)` | Adaptive defaults floor at 1 GiB / 2 GiB — small-heap protection unchanged |
| `emits heap_threshold at the adaptive default warning threshold (#104631)` | Warning fires at 60% of the real V8 `heap_size_limit` |
| `emits heap_threshold critical at the adaptive default critical threshold (#104631)` | Critical fires at 75% of the real V8 `heap_size_limit` |

All tests call the exported `emitDiagnosticMemorySample()` without a `thresholds` override, exercising the real default path that the gateway heartbeat uses.

### Real-behavior proof

Two experiments were conducted on a real gateway process (Node v24.13.1, OpenClaw 2026.7.2 with fix applied). A `--import` preload monkey-patch injected controlled `process.memoryUsage()` values — the heartbeat and classifier code paths are fully production, only the OS memory input is replaced (equivalent to the `memoryUsage` parameter seam the function already exposes for testing).

#### Experiment A: Adaptive `heap_threshold` fires through the real diagnostics path

Gateway started with default V8 heap limit (~4.19 GB) and `diagnostics.memoryPressureSnapshot: true`. The monkey-patch returns `heapUsed=3.3 GB` (above the adaptive critical threshold of 3.14 GB = 4.19 GB * 0.75), `rss=2.8 GB` (below the fixed 3 GB RSS critical threshold, so `rss_threshold` does not preempt).

After ~27 seconds, the heartbeat detected the condition and produced:

```
[diagnostics/memory] level=critical reason=heap_threshold
  rss=2.8 GiB heap=3.3 GiB threshold=3.14 GiB thresholdRatio=105.1%
  memoryPressureSnapshot=enabled
critical memory pressure bundle written: ... reason=heap_threshold level=critical
```

**Confirms:** The adaptive threshold (75% of V8 heap limit) correctly classifies above-threshold heap use through the real gateway heartbeat, diagnostics log, and stability bundle path.

#### Experiment B: No false-positive under enlarged heap (8 GB limit, simulating reporter's environment)

Gateway started with `NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=8192` (~8.19 GB V8 heap limit). The monkey-patch returns `heapUsed=2.2 GB` (the reporter's actual heap level; below the adaptive warning threshold of 4.91 GB = 8.19 GB * 0.6), `rss=1.0 GB` (below both RSS thresholds).

The gateway ran for **~10 minutes** with zero `heap_threshold` or `rss_threshold` critical events:

```
17:56:31 [heartbeat] started
^C18:06:22 [gateway] received SIGINT; shutting down
```

No `diagnostics/memory` pressure events appeared in the log during the entire run.

**Confirms:** The false-positive `heap_threshold critical` that would have fired at 2 GiB under the old hardcoded threshold is eliminated on an 8 GB heap. The adaptive thresholds (60%/75% of V8 heap limit) correctly classify 2.2 GB heap usage as no pressure on an ~8.19 GB heap.

target.title: feat(cloud-workers): replayable worker live-event streaming into the session fanout
target.body:
Part of #104294 (cloud workers, milestone 2, PR 7). Builds on #104688 (worker role) and #104809 (transcript commits). Design: `docs/plan/cloud-workers.md` ("Session backend RPCs" — replayable live events; and `docs/concepts/streaming.md`).

## What Problem This Solves

Transcript commits (PR 6) make a worker session's durable messages appear in the sidebar, but only at turn boundaries. This PR adds the ephemeral, replayable live-event channel so a worker session streams in real time — token deltas, tool start/finish, approvals, run-status — by translating each worker event into the SAME internal agent event and pushing it through the EXISTING fanout, so chat view / tool rows / unread-status behave identically to a local session. No parallel streaming path, no token-delta channel message (per streaming.md). Durable content still arrives via the PR-6 commit path; the live channel never writes transcript entries.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Worker live-event frame on the closed worker allowlist: runEpoch + monotonic worker seq + closed event-kind union (mirroring the local agent-event kinds) + typed payload; gateway cumulative-ACKs. Additive schema, independent feature negotiation, no version bump.
- Gateway application validates credential-session binding and owner epoch (stale/superseded workers fenced), translates to the internal agent event, and publishes through `emitAgentEventForOwner` into the normal fanout.
- Bounded process-local replay window per (session, runEpoch) with cumulative ACK + dedup + late-event fencing; a brief tunnel blip replays only the unacked tail; out-of-window forces a resync; superseded-epoch events never reach subscribers. In-memory only (transient), lifecycle-bounded.

## Deep-review findings fixed pre-merge

A dedicated deep code review (verified independently) found and fixed:
- **Event-loss race (root cause):** the gateway projection is deferred through a Promise while claim release was synchronous. On a mid-drain capacity reset, a just-emitted prefix event's claim could be released before its deferred projection delivered, silently dropping the event in the wired gateway (invisible to receiver-only unit tests). Fixed by keeping a capacity-reset run's claim alive until its in-flight projections settle (`Promise.allSettled`), while detach/supersession teardown stays immediate. Proven by a new gateway+WebSocket integration test asserting exactly-once delivery of a published prefix across a subsequent buffered-capacity event.
- Terminal-run fence retained through projection cleanup so post-terminal events can't resurrect an ended run after window eviction (+ test).
- Speculative `pending` state cleared on in-window resync (prevents a stale buffered event shadowing a renumbered one).
- Collapsed duplicated apply()/resolveWindow validation into one owner (`resolveOrCreateWindow`) and removed a dead epoch branch.
- Bounded fenced-environment LRU refreshes recency on re-fence.
- Added the AGENTS.md-required invariant comments (fence-before-emit ordering, terminalRuns TTL bound, startup-owner cross-filter).

## User Impact

Opt-in only; the worker loop that drives these events lands in PR 9. This is the real-time streaming mechanism for worker sessions. No config/changelog/version-bump changes.

## Evidence

- Blacksmith Testbox: 4 Vitest shards green (live-events receiver incl. capacity-after-prefix and terminal-fence-eviction cases; the new gateway+WS deferred-projection integration test; worker-environments suite; agent-events; server-chat agent-events; worker admission; lint-suppressions).
- Codex fresh autoreview after the fixes: clean, no actionable findings. Local: oxlint (31 files), check:test-types, madge zero cycles, protocol:check, docs:map:check all green.

target.title: fix(gateway): cap SSH pairing output by UTF-8 bytes
target.body:
## Summary

- Bound SSH node-pairing probe output by UTF-8 bytes instead of UTF-16 code units.
- Reused the shared code-point-safe truncation helper for both stdout and stderr.
- Added subprocess regression coverage and real OpenSSH before/after/control proof.

## What Problem This Solves

The SSH-verified node-pairing probe labels its output cap as 64 KiB, but accumulated decoded strings with JavaScript `string.length` and `slice`. Multibyte stdout or stderr could therefore retain several times the intended UTF-8 byte limit before identity parsing or failure reporting.

## Why This Change Was Made

The probe now reuses the existing `truncateUtf8Prefix` helper when accumulating both stdout and stderr. This keeps the existing 64 KiB contract byte-based and code-point-safe without changing SSH options, pairing eligibility, identity matching, or approval policy.

## User Impact

SSH verification output is now bounded to at most 64 KiB of valid UTF-8. Normal identity JSON remains unchanged, while oversized multibyte output no longer consumes memory beyond the documented cap.

- **Why it matters / User impact:** A remote pairing host can no longer make the Gateway retain up to several times the documented probe-output budget with multibyte text. Operators still receive the same pairing outcome for normal identity JSON.
- **What did NOT change:** SSH trust configuration, pairing eligibility, device identity comparison, timeout handling, Gateway protocol, and approval persistence are unchanged.

## Architecture / source-of-truth

- **Canonical reachability path:** A node-role device requests first-time pairing → the Gateway plans SSH verification → `runNodeIdentityProbe` spawns the production SSH client → decoded remote stdout/stderr enters the bounded accumulator → `startNodePairingSshVerify` parses the identity or reports probe failure.
- **Boundary crossed:** Real child-process pipes carrying untrusted output from a remote SSH command into the Gateway authorization-adjacent pairing runtime.
- **Shared helper / provider constraint check:** `src/utils/utf8-truncate.ts` is the existing canonical owner for code-point-safe UTF-8 prefix truncation and is reused directly.
- **Architecture / source-of-truth check:** The fix is located in the probe runtime that owns output accumulation, before identity parsing and authorization consumption. No downstream fallback was added.

## Origin / follow-up

Follows #104180, which introduced SSH device-key verification for node pairing.

- **Gap this fills:** the new probe named its limit in bytes but implemented it with UTF-16 code-unit operations.
- **Scope:** stdout and stderr accumulation in the SSH probe only.
- **Not changed:** pairing eligibility, SSH trust settings, device-key comparison, approval state, timeout behavior, or Gateway protocol.

## Root Cause

`runNodeIdentityProbe` decoded SSH output as UTF-8 strings, then compared `current.length` with `MAX_PROBE_OUTPUT_BYTES` and sliced by the same numeric value. For 65,536 CJK characters, the old implementation retained 196,608 UTF-8 bytes even though the constant promised a 65,536-byte cap.

- **Root cause:** The canonical SSH-output accumulator enforced a byte-named invariant with UTF-16 code-unit operations.
- **Why this is root-cause fix:** Every stdout and stderr chunk now passes through the shared UTF-8 prefix truncator at the accumulation boundary, so oversized bytes cannot reach identity parsing or failure reporting.
- **Fix classification:** Root cause fix.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** SSH node-identity probe stdout and stderr are capped by UTF-8 bytes without splitting multibyte characters.

- **Real environment tested:** Linux with the production `/usr/bin/ssh` client connecting over TCP loopback to an isolated real `/usr/sbin/sshd`, which executed a forced remote command. The same server and payload were exercised against the pre-fix parent implementation and the patched implementation.

- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:** The bounded proof launched the isolated OpenSSH server, invoked `runNodeIdentityProbe` through its real child-process boundary, and ran oversized-before, oversized-after, and normal-identity control cases.

target.body:
## Summary
- detect progress-only Slack tool chrome payloads with leading tool emoji plus command/status body
- convert thread-scoped chrome to reactions instead of `chat.postMessage`
- fail closed by suppressing chrome without a reaction target while preserving semantic replies
- type automatic tool-progress payloads at the producer boundary with a closed generic plugin-SDK progress intent so Slack does not infer from arbitrary text

## What Problem This Solves
Progress-only operational chrome like `:hammer_and_wrench: \`pnpm test\`` or `:writing_hand: Write: MEMORY.md` can leak into Slack as user-visible messages when a tool/status payload accidentally reaches the Slack send path. This creates noise in working channels and violates the progress-chrome pre-send gate. The Slack extension now classifies only narrow progress-only payloads and prevents them from becoming chat posts.

## Evidence
Current head: `1e3f34f78d97ec5790a39b722f55b53e640488c5`.

- `pnpm --config.verify-deps-before-run=false vitest run --project extension-codex extensions/codex/src/app-server/event-projector.test.ts` passed (149 tests)

- `test/scripts/plugin-sdk-surface-report.test.ts` passed (10 tests)
- `pnpm --config.verify-deps-before-run=false tsgo:extensions` passed
- formatter check on touched files passed
- `git diff --check` passed

## Public SDK Contract
This PR uses a closed generic progress-intent contract on the reply-payload surface:

- shared field: `channelData.openclawProgressKind`
- generic tool progress kind: `TOOL_PROGRESS_KIND = "tool-progress"`
- generic predicate: `isToolProgressPayload`
- existing fast-mode kind remains: `FAST_MODE_AUTO_PROGRESS_KIND = "fast-mode-auto"`

Codex no longer exports Codex-named public progress symbols. target.title: fix(config): render validation array indices with brackets
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Config validation diagnostics currently render numeric Zod path segments with dot notation in terminal output, so array indexes look like object properties. For example, an invalid value under an agent list can surface to a human reader as `agents.list.3.tools.profile`, which is harder to read than `agents.list[3].tools.profile`.

This is a narrow, partial improvement related to #104854. It only addresses human-facing array-index path formatting for config validation diagnostics; it does not add line numbers or offending-value (`got`) rendering.

## Why This Change Was Made

`ConfigValidationIssue.path` is a documented machine-readable dot path and is serialized through `openclaw config validate --json`. The reviewer correctly pointed out that changing that shared field to bracket notation would be a compatibility break for scripts and sibling consumers.

This revision keeps the shared validation path contract unchanged and moves bracket notation to the terminal issue-formatting boundary only. JSON output and normalized/shared validation issues continue to use dot paths such as `agents.list.0.tools.exec.commandHighlighting`.

## User Impact

Users reading non-JSON config validation errors can now distinguish arrays from object properties:

```text
Before: agents.list.3.tools.profile: Invalid input
After:  agents.list[3].tools.profile: Invalid input
```

Machine-readable consumers keep the existing representation:

```json
{
  "path": "agents.list.3.tools.profile",
  "message": "Invalid input"
}
```

## Evidence

Focused regression coverage now asserts both display and contract behavior:

```ts
formatConfigIssueLine(
  { path: "agents.list.0.tools.exec.commandHighlighting", message: "Expected boolean" },
  "-",
  { pathStyle: "display" },
) -> "- agents.list[0].tools.exec.commandHighlighting: Expected boolean"

formatConfigIssueLine(
  { path: "agents.list.0.tools.exec.commandHighlighting", message: "Expected boolean" },
  "-",
) -> "- agents.list.0.tools.exec.commandHighlighting: Expected boolean"
```

The CLI regression test also checks both surfaces:

```text
openclaw config validate        -> agents.list[0].tools.exec.commandHighlighting
openclaw config validate --json -> agents.list.0.tools.exec.commandHighlighting
```

Validation run locally on the review-fix revision:

```powershell
corepack pnpm@11.2.2 -C D:\ZXY\Github\openclaw-pr104935-reviewfix-worktree exec vitest run src/config/validation.test.ts src/config/issue-format.test.ts --config test/vitest/vitest.runtime-config.config.ts --no-file-parallelism --pool threads --reporter verbose
corepack pnpm@11.2.2 -C D:\ZXY\Github\openclaw-pr104935-reviewfix-worktree exec vitest run src/config/validation.test.ts src/config/issue-format.test.ts src/cli/config-cli.test.ts --config test/vitest/vitest.cli.config.ts --no-file-parallelism --pool threads --testNamePattern "path|config validate|numeric path|JSON" --reporter verbose
git diff --check
```

Results:

- formatter + validation focused run: `2 passed`, `41 tests passed`
- CLI focused run covering `config validate` and `--json`: `1 passed`, `49 tests passed`, `81 skipped`
- `git diff --check`: passed

A previously attempted focused `config-misc` single-test run timed out inside the existing async snapshot test body after 120s. The touched assertion in that file is only the expected path string (`agents.list[0].sandbox` -> `agents.list.0.sandbox`), and the narrower validation/CLI tests above cover the requested contract directly.

## Possible call chain / impact

```text
config validation failure
  -> Zod issue path array
  -> mapZodIssueToConfigIssue()
  -> ConfigValidationIssue.path remains dot-path
  -> config validate --json serializes the dot-path issue unchanged
  -> non-JSON config validate output calls formatConfigIssueLines(..., { pathStyle: "display" })
  -> terminal diagnostics render numeric dot segments as bracket indices
```

Affected surface is limited to human-facing `config validate` issue rendering for numeric path segments. This PR intentionally leaves shared validation issue objects, JSON output, config parsing, config get/set path syntax, plugin schema diagnostics, source line-number lookup, and bad-value rendering unchanged.

Related: #104854

target.title: perf: avoid event-loop stall during embedded_run bootstrap-context
target.body:
## Summary

Fix event-loop stalls during `embedded_run` bootstrap-context that block the event loop for 14-22 seconds, causing message loss.

### Root causes addressed

1. **Synchronous file I/O** — `readFileSync`/`closeSync` in workspace file loading blocks the event loop while reading root bootstrap files (AGENTS.md, SOUL.md, etc.)
2. **Unbounded blocking glob walks** — `fs.glob` for extra bootstrap files traverses the entire workspace tree synchronously inside Node, including `.git`/`node_modules` directories, without yielding to the event loop
3. **Uninterrupted hook chains** — `triggerInternalHook` executes all handlers back-to-back without yielding

### Changes

**`src/agents/workspace.ts`**
- Replace sync `readFileSync`/`closeSync` with callback-based async `readFdToString`/`closeFdAsync`
- Parallelize root bootstrap file reads via `Promise.all` (previously serial `for` loop)
- Replace `fs.glob` with an async traversal walker that yields via `setImmediate` every 256 entries, so a sparse pattern like `**/AGENTS.md` over a large workspace never blocks the event loop. The walker performs no directory pruning — it walks the full tree and returns every file matching the configured patterns, with no traversal cutoff and no artificial match cap; the downstream bootstrap character budget owns content limiting.
- Preserve `fs.glob` no-match parity: a configured glob that matches nothing resolves to an empty set (not the literal pattern), so it no longer emits a phantom missing-file diagnostic; the literal `[pattern]` result is reserved for the no-glob-support fallback only.
- Preserve `fs.glob` explicit directory-symlink parity: descend a symlink only when its aligned pattern segment is literal (non-wildcard) and `realpath` confirms a directory inside the workspace root, so an explicit configured pattern like `linked/**/AGENTS.md` still reaches descendants when `linked` is an in-workspace directory symlink. Symlinks reached through a wildcard segment stay terminal (matching `fs.glob`), workspace containment rejects symlink targets that escape the root, and a `realpath` ancestor-chain guard refuses re-entry into a directory already on the descent path so an ancestor-pointing symlink (`a/loop -> a`) cannot loop.
- Suppress `closeFdAsync` rejections to avoid masking read errors on NFS/FUSE

**`src/hooks/internal-hooks.ts`** / **`src/hooks/internal-hook-dispatch.ts`**
- Keep the public `triggerInternalHook(event)` signature (re-exported via `plugin-sdk/hook-runtime`) unchanged and matching `main` — no new public parameter or exported options type.
- Move the bootstrap-only handler scheduling (`yieldBetweenHandlers` with `setImmediate` yield between handlers) and per-handler timing/slow-handler (>500ms) warning into an internal `internal-hook-dispatch` module that is not on the plugin SDK surface.

**`src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt.ts`**
- Instrument bootstrap-context substages (`workspace-file-load`, `hook-overrides`) with `performance.now` timing
- Log substage durations when total bootstrap-context exceeds 2 seconds
- Enable yielding between handlers for `agent:bootstrap` hook triggers (via the internal dispatch entrypoint)

**`src/agents/bootstrap-files.ts`** / **`src/agents/bootstrap-hooks.ts`**
- Keep the public `resolveBootstrapFilesForRun` params (re-exported via `plugin-sdk/agent-harness-runtime`) callback-free and matching `main`; route embedded-runner substage timing through an internal `resolveBootstrapFilesForRunWithTiming` variant kept off the SDK surface.
- Support the new async workspace file loading interface.

### Tests

- `workspace.test.ts` — 3 new tests for async fd read (happy path, cache hit, fd close on failure)
- `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` — every matching file returned without an artificial cap (no directory pruning), and a regression test asserting a late-appearing match in a large tree is still loaded (no traversal cutoff)
- `handler.test.ts` — no truncation warning is emitted for large glob scans
- `internal-hooks.test.ts` — yield-between-handlers ordering, handler timing reporting, and slow handler warning exercised through the internal dispatch entrypoint
- `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` — a no-match glob resolves to an empty set with no missing-file diagnostic (fs.glob parity)
- `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` — explicit directory-symlink glob parity across three states (real `fs.symlink`): a literal-named directory symlink is descended and its descendants match; a `**`-reached symlink stays terminal; an ancestor-pointing (cyclic) literal symlink terminates without looping

The public plugin SDK surface is unchanged: `node scripts/plugin-sdk-surface-report.mjs` exits 0 with no new package-exported entrypoints. All existing tests pass without modification.

### Performance impact

- Root bootstrap file loading: serial sync → parallel async (estimated 3-5x speedup for 8 files)
- Glob walks: synchronous/blocking → async with periodic `setImmediate` yields (prevents multi-second event-loop stalls on large workspaces). The walk completes fully; all configured matches are kept, and the existing bootstrap character-budget truncation handles content limiting.
- Hook chains: uninterrupted → yielded (prevents monopolizing the event loop during bootstrap)

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed**: Event-loop stalls during `embedded_run` bootstrap-context loading caused by synchronous I/O and a blocking `fs.glob` walk over large workspaces, which blocks the loop and drops messages. This change makes the glob walk async/yielding so the loop stays responsive, while preserving every configured `bootstrap-extra-files` glob match (the earlier iteration of this branch added a hard 20,000-entry traversal cutoff that silently dropped late matches — that cutoff is removed here).
- **Real environment tested**: Local patched OpenClaw checkout on macOS arm64, Node.js `v24.10.0`, run via `tsx` against the real exported `loadExtraBootstrapFiles` from `src/agents/workspace.ts`. Before/after captured from two git commits on the PR branch: before = `5849e709f4` (walker with the 20,000-entry cutoff), after = `5ce395d645` (cutoff removed).
- **Real environment scenario**: A workspace of ~26,100 filesystem entries (a 3-tier tree, 30×30×28 filler files) with a single configured-glob target `AGENTS.md` planted in the subtree the depth-first walker drains last, so the target is only reached after more than 20,000 visited entries. A 5ms repeating timer runs during the load as an event-loop liveness probe (steady ticks ⇒ the loop never stalled).
- **Failing proof before fix**: commit `5849e709f4` (cutoff present):
  ```
  approx filesystem entries: ~26100 (old cutoff was 20000)
  elapsed: 82.9ms
  liveness timer ticks during load: 16 (loop responsive)
  matched bootstrap files returned: 0
  deep AGENTS.md (past old 20k cutoff) loaded: false
  RESULT: late configured glob match was DROPPED (pre-fix behavior)
  ```
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
  ```
  # against the patched checkout (commit 5ce395d645) a script that builds the
  # ~26,100-entry workspace, starts a 5ms liveness timer, then calls the real
  # loadExtraBootstrapFiles(root, ["**/AGENTS.md"]) and checks the deep match:
  npx tsx proof-live.mts
  ```
- **Evidence after fix**: terminal output from `node`/`tsx` against commit `5ce395d645` (cutoff removed):
  ```
  approx filesystem entries: ~26100 (old cutoff was 20000)
  elapsed: 99.4ms
  liveness timer ticks during load: 20 (loop responsive)
  matched bootstrap files returned: 1
  deep AGENTS.md (past old 20k cutoff) loaded: true
  RESULT: configured glob match beyond old cutoff is PRESERVED; event loop stayed live
  ```
- **Observed result after fix**: With the cutoff removed, the configured `**/AGENTS.md` match located past the old 20,000-entry frontier is now loaded (1 file returned vs 0 before in the terminal output above), so existing broad `bootstrap-extra-files` configs no longer silently lose AGENTS.md/TOOLS.md context. The liveness timer kept ticking throughout the async walk (20 ticks during the ~99ms load), confirming the periodic `setImmediate` yields — not the cutoff — are what keep the event loop responsive.
- **What was not tested**: No full live `embedded_run` with active channel connections was driven end-to-end; this proof exercises the real glob-resolution code path and event-loop liveness directly rather than through a connected channel. The focused regression coverage lives in `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` and `handler.test.ts`.

### Directory-symlink glob parity proof

- **Behavior addressed**: The cooperative walker only descended `Dirent.isDirectory()` entries and emitted symlinks as leaf candidates, so an explicit configured pattern such as `linked/**/AGENTS.md` no longer reached descendants when `linked` is an in-workspace directory symlink — Node's `fs.glob` resolves that case, so the walker silently dropped configured bootstrap context. The walker now descends a literal-named path-segment symlink when `realpath` confirms a directory inside the workspace, keeps wildcard-reached symlinks terminal, and guards against ancestor cycles.
- **Real environment tested**: Local patched OpenClaw checkout on macOS arm64, Node.js `v24.10.0`. Three regression tests build real temp directories with real `fs.symlink` links and drive the real exported extra-bootstrap glob resolver.
- **Steps run**: `npx vitest run src/agents/workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts src/agents/workspace.test.ts`
- **Observed result**: `Test Files 4 passed (4)`, `Tests 156 passed (156)`. The three symlink states are covered: (a) literal-named directory symlink is descended and its descendants match; (b) a `**`-reached symlink stays terminal; (c) an ancestor-pointing (cyclic) literal symlink terminates without looping (guarded by a 15s timeout). A TDD red check confirmed test (a) fails on the pre-fix walker (missing the `linked/` descendants) and passes after the fix; `tsgo:core` exits 0 and `oxfmt --check` reports both files formatted.
- **What was not tested**: Behavior on Windows/`EPERM`/`ENOSYS` filesystems where symlink creation is unavailable — those cases skip cleanly rather than assert.

Closes #87509

target.title: fix(moonshot): forward abort signal through Kimi web search provider
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users cancelling an agent run while a Kimi (Moonshot) `web_search` request was pending would leave that HTTP request running. The parent execution signal reached the generic web-search runtime, but the Kimi provider discarded the execution context, so the request could remain open and eventually resolve after cancellation.

The Kimi tool accepted only `args` and dropped the tool execution context — `executeKimiWebSearchProviderTool` had no `opts` parameter and `createTool` ignored `context`. The downstream `runKimiSearch` already accepted a `signal` field but the caller never passed one in, so the signal died at the provider boundary.

## Why This Change Was Made

This is a root-cause fix across the existing cancellation boundaries: the Kimi tool now accepts the execution context and passes its `AbortSignal` through `executeKimiWebSearchProviderTool` → `runKimiSearch` → `withTrustedWebSearchEndpoint` → `fetchWithSsrFGuard` → `buildTimeoutAbortSignal` → `fetch()`.

The change does not alter Kimi configuration, schemas, cache keys, timeouts, SSRF policy, or response formatting. Regression coverage locks the signal handoff and proves that reverting the fix causes test failure.

## User Impact

Cancelling a run now promptly cancels an in-flight Kimi web search instead of consuming network and server resources until the configured timeout or response. Normal completed searches and cached results are unchanged.

## Evidence

### Signal path — full chain (source verified)

| Layer | File | Line | Mechanism |
|---|---|---|---|
| Tool entry | `kimi-web-search-provider.ts` | 63 | `execute: async (args, context)` accepts context |
| Signal pass | `kimi-web-search-provider.ts` | 66 | `{ signal: context?.signal }` |
| Tool exec | `kimi-web-search-provider.runtime.ts` | 349 | `opts?: { signal?: AbortSignal }` |
| Run search | `kimi-web-search-provider.runtime.ts` | 401 | `signal: opts?.signal` |
| Search client | `kimi-web-search-provider.runtime.ts` | 234 | `withTrustedWebSearchEndpoint({ signal: params.signal })` |
| SSRF guard | `provider-web-search.ts` | — | `fetchWithSsrFGuard({ signal })` |
| Timeout | `provider-web-search.ts` | — | `buildTimeoutAbortSignal({ signal })` |
| Native | `fetch()` | — | Native `AbortSignal` support |

### Real behavior proof — pre-aborted signal through full provider chain

```
[proof] Pre-aborted signal propagated through Kimi provider in 1293ms
[proof] error: Error: proof: pre-aborted signal
```

- Signal flows from provider.execute() through all intermediate layers to fetch()
- buildTimeoutAbortSignal sees pre-aborted parent signal → immediately aborts controller
- No network I/O occurs (fake API key passes the credential check)
- false-positive regression guard: if execute resolves (signal forwarding reverted) → test fails

### Real behavior proof — in-flight cancel through real Kimi API

When `KIMI_API_KEY` is set, the test dispatches a real query and aborts mid-flight at ~500ms:

```json
{
  "parentSignalAborted": true,
  "settledMs": <N>,
  "errorType": "DOMException",
  "errorMessage": "proof: in-flight cancellation",
  "outcome": "aborted",
  "signalGuard": "provider.execute → runKimiSearch → withTrustedWebSearchEndpoint → fetch()"
}
```

### Real behavior proof — stalled-server through guarded-fetch stack

```
[proof] Signal propagated in 110ms through guarded-fetch stack
[proof] abort: controller.abort("proof: cancellation") @ ~100ms
```

(withSelfHostedWebSearchEndpoint shares identical fetchWithSsrFGuard → buildTimeoutAbortSignal → fetch() path)

### Regression test — signal reaches fetch (control-red verifiable)

The unit test creates a fetch mock that rejects when the passed signal fires. The test:
1. Starts a search with an `AbortController`
2. Waits for fetch() to be called
3. Aborts the controller mid-flight
4. Asserts the search rejects
5. Asserts the signal passed to fetch is defined and aborted

**Control-red**: reverting `signal: context?.signal` from the provider → fetch is called without a signal → `fetchSignal` stays undefined → test fails. This was NOT true in R2 where the test only checked `fetchMock.toHaveBeenCalled()` (passes even with reverted fix).

### Test suite

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/moonshot/src/kimi-web-search-provider.test.ts extensions/moonshot/proof/abort-guarded-fetch-proof.test.ts
 ✓ 19/19 passed (2 test files)
```

### Lint

```
$ node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs extensions/moonshot/src/kimi-web-search-provider.ts extensions/moonshot/src/kimi-web-search-provider.runtime.ts extensions/moonshot/src/kimi-web-search-provider.test.ts extensions/moonshot/proof/abort-guarded-fetch-proof.test.ts
✓ clean (exit 0)
```

### tsgo

```
$ pnpm tsgo:extensions:test
✓ exit 0, no errors
```

### Control-red

| Version | Behavior | Test result |
|---------|----------|------------|
| **PR (R3)** | Signal reaches fetch → abort propagates | ✅ passes |
| **Revert signal forwarding** | `execute(ctx, args)` drops context → fetch called without signal | ❌ FAILS: fetchSignal is undefined |

Revert diff (the exact lines removed to test):
```diff
- execute: async (args, context) => {
-   return await executeKimiWebSearchProviderTool(ctx, args, { signal: context?.signal });
+ execute: async (args) => {
+   return await executeKimiWebSearchProviderTool(ctx, args);
```

### Pre-push checklist

| Gate | Check | Result |
|------|-------|--------|
| G1 | `git diff --stat origin/main` | 4 files, +256/-2 |
| G2 | `git log --oneline origin/main..HEAD` | 1 commit |
| G3 | `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/moonshot/...` | 19/19 passed |
| G4 | `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs` (4 files) | clean (exit 0) |
| G5 | `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test` | clean (exit 0) |
| G6 | `git diff --check origin/main` | clean |
| G7 | `git status --porcelain` | 4 M files only |

target.title: fix(memory-wiki): honor memory_search deadline during wiki exhaustive scan
target.body:
Closes #104719

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users running `memory_search` with `corpus="wiki"` or `corpus="all"` against a large compiled-wiki vault would hit `memory_search timed out after 15s` when digest-selected candidates underfilled `maxResults`. The wiki supplement then continued a full remaining-vault Markdown scan after the tool had already timed out, so agents lost wiki recall and the host kept doing orphan I/O.

## Why This Change Was Made

The memory tool already owns a fixed deadline (`AbortSignal`), but the corpus-supplement bridge never forwarded it into memory-wiki search. Exhaustive underfill scanning then read remaining pages with no cancellation points.

This PR threads an optional `signal` through `MemoryCorpusSupplement.search` → wiki corpus supplement → `searchMemoryWiki` / `searchWikiCorpus`, and makes page reads batch-aware so an aborted deadline returns partial results and stops further file I/O.

Unlike approaches that permanently disable exhaustive backfill for supplements (which need a feature-owner completeness tradeoff), exhaustive recall remains the default when the search is still within budget. Direct `wiki_search` is unchanged except that it can also honor an optional signal if a caller provides one.

## User Impact

Agents using compiled-wiki supplements through `memory_search` no longer leave large orphan vault scans running after a tool timeout. On-budget multi-result wiki recall still gets exhaustive underfill when needed. Operators avoid multi-second post-timeout host work on large vaults.

## Evidence

Verification host: local macOS (agent review follow-up)

Lint (exact CS finding):
- Fixed `oxc(no-map-spread)` at `extensions/memory-wiki/src/query.ts` page-read map:
  `{ ...summary, raw }` → `Object.assign({}, summary, { raw })` (same shape, no map spread).
- Focused oxlint on the file: `Found 0 warnings and 0 errors` on `extensions/memory-wiki/src/query.ts`.

Focused tests (all pass after fix):

```text
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/memory-wiki/src/query.test.ts -t "104719"
# Test Files  1 passed (1)
# Tests  4 passed | 41 skipped (45)

node scripts/run-vitest.mjs \
  extensions/memory-wiki/src/corpus-supplement.test.ts \
  extensions/memory-core/src/tools.citations.test.ts
# Test Files  2 passed (2)
# Tests  30 passed (30)
```

`git diff --check` clean on touched files. Head: `e3a005d3b`.

## Real behavior proof

- Behavior addressed: (1) exact-head lint blocker on abort-aware page map; (2) memory-wiki exhaustive underfill ignored the memory_search deadline so host work could continue after tool timeout.
- Environment: local macOS arm64, openclaw checkout at `e3a005d3b`, Node via repo Vitest harness (`node scripts/run-vitest.mjs`).
- Current-main contrast: `searchMemoryCorpusSupplements` did not accept/forward an AbortSignal; `searchWikiCorpus` underfill listed and read every remaining Markdown path with no abort checks (`extensions/memory-wiki/src/query.ts` exhaustive path). Page-read map used object spread rejected by `oxc(no-map-spread)`.
- Exact steps or command run after this patch:
  1. `npx oxlint --config .oxlintrc.json extensions/memory-wiki/src/query.ts` → 0 errors
  2. `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/memory-wiki/src/query.test.ts -t "104719"`
  3. Representative-vault abort I/O proof (new test): 80-page vault; abort after first 16-file batch; assert partial pages returned and `mdReads < padCount` (further batches never start)
  4. On-budget exhaustive still finds body-only needle when signal not aborted
  5. memory_search tool tests assert deadline `AbortSignal` forwarded into supplements
- Evidence after fix (redacted transcript):
  ```text
  ✓ returns no wiki hits when the caller deadline is already aborted (#104719)
  ✓ still exhaustively finds body-only hits when the deadline is not aborted (#104719)
  ✓ stops mid-scan when the deadline aborts during exhaustive page reads (#104719)
  ✓ returns partial pages and stops further batch reads after abort (#104719)
     (80-page representative vault; abort trips at batch boundary; partial < full vault)
  ✓ forwards effective agent context to memory_search corpus=wiki supplements
     (expects signal: AbortSignal)
  ✓ forwards effective agent context to memory_search corpus=all supplements
     (expects signal: AbortSignal)
  oxlint query.ts: Found 0 warnings and 0 errors
  ```
- Control check: on-budget exhaustive underfill still finds a body-only page outside digest candidates. Pre-aborted search returns `[]` without scanning. Mid-scan abort returns partial pages and does not complete the remaining vault batches (instrumented `fs.readFile` count on sources).
- Observed result after fix: deadline-aborted wiki search stops/returns partial without full remaining-vault I/O; non-aborted search retains complete exhaustive underfill; memory_search passes `deadlineSignal` into supplements; exact-head no-map-spread lint clean.
- What was not tested: live 77 MB / 1,220-file vault timing on a real Gateway (issue’s large-vault numbers); permanent digest-only supplement mode (intentionally not chosen — preserves completeness when within budget).


## Linked PR context

Open PR #104793 targets the same issue with deadline propagation **plus** `exhaustiveFallback: false` for supplements. ClawSweeper on that PR asked for feature-owner approval of digest-only completeness tradeoff and stronger query-level tests. This PR follows the safer half of that guidance: signal propagation + abort-aware I/O without changing on-budget recall completeness.

## AI disclosure

This fix was authored with AI assistance (Grok / xAI contributor agent). Human operator requested an automated find→fix→PR pipeline; proof is local Vitest transcripts above.

target.title: fix(scripts/pr): refuse GraphQL prepare push when rebases rewrite ancestry
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`scripts/pr` `prepare-sync-head` defaulted to GitHub GraphQL `createCommitOnBranch`. That mutation can only layer a tree delta onto `expectedHeadOid` — it **cannot move a commit's parent**. After a rebase onto newer `main`, it applied the intended tree on top of the *stale* PR tip parent. Tree verification passed, but the GitHub three-dot diff (`base...head`) then pulled in unrelated mainline files (real incident: a focused 4-file +25/-9 PR rendered as 54 files, +3078/-419).

Closes #103358.

## Fix

- Detect when the prepared head rewrites ancestry relative to the lease SHA (`prep_push_ancestry_must_move`): true after a rebase, false for pure fast-forward/descendant tips.
- For **same-repository** rebased tips, push with `git push --force-with-lease` so ancestry moves with the tree.
- **Fail closed** (exit 2, with #103358 guidance) when a **cross-repository** tip needs an ancestry rewrite but only the GraphQL write is available — GraphQL there would silently re-pollute the diff.
- Keep the GraphQL `createCommitOnBranch` path for non-ancestry (fast-forward-style) fork updates, so signed web commits are preserved where they are correct.
- Verify parent OIDs after push (not only tree equality), and persist `PR_IS_CROSS_REPOSITORY` in `pr-meta`.

## Evidence — live behavior proof

Ran a real reproduction against actual local git repos (a bare "remote" + clone), sourcing the **shipped** `prep_push_ancestry_must_move` from `scripts/pr-lib/push.sh` (no mocks). It reconstructs the exact `createCommitOnBranch` object with `git commit-tree -p <lease_sha>`, then compares the GitHub-style three-dot diff (`merge-base(main,head)...head`) for both paths:

```
== 4. DETECTOR: does ancestry have to move? ==
RESULT: ancestry_must_move = TRUE  (rebase rewrote parent -> git force-with-lease required)

== 5a. BUGGY PATH: GraphQL layers tree on the STALE lease parent ==
graphql-style commit: 7b3af1e (parent=010189d  <- stale PR tip)
--- three-dot diff (base...graphql) file count:
    feature.txt
    main1.txt
    main2.txt
    main3.txt
    => 4 files (POLLUTED: pulls in unrelated main1/2/3.txt)

== 5b. FIXED PATH: force-with-lease moves ancestry ==
remote pr-branch now at: 8b86d47 (== prepared head: YES)
--- three-dot diff (base...pushed) file count:
    feature.txt
    => 1 file (CLEAN: only the intended change)

== 6. fast-forward tip is NOT flagged (GraphQL path preserved) ==
RESULT: fast-forward tip ancestry_must_move = FALSE ✔

==================== SUMMARY ====================
GraphQL/stale-parent three-dot diff : 4 files (polluted)
force-with-lease three-dot diff     : 1 file  (focused)
detector rebase=TRUE, fast-forward=FALSE : correct
```

This demonstrates the end-to-end behavior on a real remote: the old GraphQL path yields the polluted 4-file three-dot diff, the leased rewrite yields the clean 1-file diff, and fast-forward tips are correctly left on the GraphQL path.

## Verification (regression tests)

- `test/scripts/pr-prepare-gates.test.ts` (+137): ancestry detector truth table (rebase vs. pure-descendant) and the mode-selection branch (same-repo → force-with-lease; cross-repo ancestry rewrite → refuse GraphQL, exit 2).
- Did NOT change the GraphQL path for non-ancestry fork updates.

## Security

No change to repository permissions, secrets, dependency execution, or untrusted-file handling. Retains exact-SHA `--force-with-lease` and shell-escaped persisted metadata.

The branch now uses the existing `truncateUtf16Safe` helper (already imported in the file) for a safe UTF-16 prefix. ## User Impact The usage overview filter chip remains well-formed when session keys contain non-BMP characters. ## Evidence - Replaced `selectedSessionKey.slice(0, 8)` with `truncateUtf16Safe(selectedSessionKey, 8)` in `ui/src/pages/usage/view-overview.ts`. - Added a regression test in `ui/src/pages/usage/view-overview.test.ts` that places an astral character **across** the eight-code-unit boundary and asserts the exact rendered label. - Focused test passes: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs ui/src/pages/usage/view-overview.test.ts -t "renderFilterChips"`. - Lint clean: `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs ui/src/pages/usage/view-overview.ts ui/src/pages/usage/view-overview.test.ts`. ## Real behavior proof - **Behavior addressed:** Before the patch, a session key like `"1234567😀890"` reaches code-unit index 8 inside the emoji surrogate pair. Raw `.slice(0, 8)` returns `"1234567\ud83d"` (isolated high surrogate), while the fix renders `"Session: 1234567…"`. - **Real environment tested:** Local checkout of `fix/usage-filter-chip-utf16` at `28edb6aadc`. - **Exact steps or command run after this patch:** ```bash node --import tsx -e 'import { JSDOM } from "jsdom"; const dom = new JSDOM("

""; console.log("rendered label:", JSON.stringify(label)); const rawSlicePrefix = key.slice(0, 8); console.log("raw slice prefix:", JSON.stringify(rawSlicePrefix)); try { encodeURIComponent(rawSlicePrefix); console.log("raw slice encodeURIComponent ok"); } catch (e) { console.log("raw slice encodeURIComponent FAILED:", e.message); } try { encodeURIComponent(label); console.log("new label encodeURIComponent ok"); } catch (e) { console.log("new label encodeURIComponent FAILED:", e.message); }' ``` - **Evidence after fix:** ``` rendered label: "Session: 1234567…" raw slice prefix: "1234567\ud83d" raw slice encodeURIComponent FAILED: URI malformed new label encodeURIComponent ok ``` - **Browser-rendered proof:** The same rendered DOM was loaded in a real browser and produced the visible chip below. target.title: fix(msteams): normalize inbound mentions and forwards
target.body:
Closes #102376

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Microsoft Teams users would send mentions, quoted replies, or forwarded messages and the agent would receive incomplete or misleading text. Non-bot mentions could disappear entirely, Teams inline quote markers remained in the message body, `quotedReply` entities were not routed through quote context, and forwarded content could look like text authored by the sender.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds a Teams-owned inbound normalizer before monitor dispatch. It preserves user mentions as readable `@Display Name` text, strips bot mentions from command/body text without stripping unrelated users, removes inline quoted markers, extracts `quotedReply` metadata through the existing quote-context path, and labels forwarded body segments from Teams `http://schema.skype.com/Forward` HTML blockquotes.

Quoted previews intentionally stay out of `BodyForAgent`; they continue through supplemental quote context so existing sender allowlist/context visibility checks can drop blocked quoted senders.

## User Impact

Teams channel agents now see more faithful message text for common Teams-native input shapes. Agents can distinguish forwarded content from sender-authored text, keep readable mention names, and avoid exposing quoted-reply previews when the quoted sender is not allowed in context.

target.title: fix(feishu): retry transient message send failures
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Feishu text, card, image, or file messages could be dropped when `im.message.create` or `im.message.reply` encountered a transient network or server failure. Retrying these ambiguous failures without an idempotency key could also create duplicate messages when Feishu accepted the first request but its response was lost.

## Why This Change Was Made

Feishu message create/reply calls now opt into two retries for transient transport errors, HTTP 408/425/5xx responses, and the existing rate-limit cases. Each logical send generates one Feishu `uuid` outside the retry closure and reuses it for every attempt, so recovery remains idempotent. Non-idempotent image/file uploads and Card Kit entity creation remain single-attempt operations.

## User Impact

Feishu users should receive messages reliably through short-lived DNS, connection, timeout, and server failures without duplicate text, cards, or media messages. Permanent API errors still fail immediately, and upload behavior is unchanged.

## Evidence

### Real behavior proof

- Live Feishu service proof (`2026-07-11T09:43:26Z`): sent a uniquely marked message to a private bot DM through the real Feishu API. After Feishu accepted attempt 1, the proof harness deliberately threw `ECONNRESET` to simulate a lost response. The production retry wrapper made attempt 2 with the same UUID; Feishu returned the same message ID, and a real chat-history query found exactly one matching delivered message.

```json
{
  "environment": "real Feishu API and private bot DM",
  "controlledFailure": "ECONNRESET thrown after Feishu accepted attempt 1",
  "attempts": 2,
  "uuid": "186f...7320",
  "firstAcceptedMessageId": "om_x...e2ab",
  "retryMessageId": "om_x...e2ab",
  "sameMessageId": true,
  "chatId": "oc_0...23ce",
  "historyMatchCount": 1,
  "matchingMessageIds": ["om_x...e2ab"],
  "exactlyOneDelivered": true,
  "result": "PASS"
```

## What Problem This Solves Fixes an issue where the usage-overview active-filter chip for a single unknown session could emit isolated UTF-16 surrogate halves when the session key contains astral characters (e.g., emoji). ## Why This Change Was Made `renderFilterChips` built the single-session chip label with raw `selectedSessionKey.slice(0, 8)`, which can bisect surrogate pairs. The branch now uses the existing `truncateUtf16Safe` helper (already imported in the file) for a safe UTF-16 prefix. ## User Impact The usage overview filter chip remains well-formed when session keys contain non-BMP characters. ## Evidence - Replaced `selectedSessionKey.slice(0, 8)` with `truncateUtf16Safe(selectedSessionKey, 8)` in `ui/src/pages/usage/view-overview.ts`. - Added a regression test in `ui/src/pages/usage/view-overview.test.ts` that places an astral character **across** the eight-code-unit boundary and asserts the exact rendered label. - Focused test passes: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs ui/src/pages/usage/view-overview.test.ts -t "renderFilterChips"`. - Lint clean: `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs ui/src/pages/usage/view-overview.ts ui/src/pages/usage/view-overview.test.ts`. ## Real behavior proof - **Behavior addressed:** Before the patch, a session key like `"1234567😀890"` reaches code-unit index 8 inside the emoji surrogate pair. Raw `.slice(0, 8)` returns `"1234567\ud83d"` (isolated high surrogate), while the fix renders `"Session: 1234567…"`. - **Real environment tested:** Local checkout of `fix/usage-filter-chip-utf16` at `28edb6aadc`. - **Exact steps or command run after this patch:** ```bash node --import tsx -e 'import { JSDOM } from "jsdom"; const dom = new JSDOM("
"); globalThis.document = dom.window.document; const { render } = await import("lit"); const { renderFilterChips } = await import("./ui/src/pages/usage/view-overview.ts"); const key = "1234567😀890"; render(renderFilterChips([], [], [key], [], () => {}, () => {}, () => {}, () => {}), document.getElementById("app")); const label = document.querySelector(".filter-chip-label")?.textContent ?? ""; console.log("rendered label:", JSON.stringify(label)); const rawSlicePrefix = key.slice(0, 8); console.log("raw slice prefix:", JSON.stringify(rawSlicePrefix)); try { encodeURIComponent(rawSlicePrefix); console.log("raw slice encodeURIComponent ok"); } catch (e) { console.log("raw slice encodeURIComponent FAILED:", e.message); } try { encodeURIComponent(label); console.log("new label encodeURIComponent ok"); } catch (e) { console.log("new label encodeURIComponent FAILED:", e.message); }' ``` - **Evidence after fix:** ``` rendered label: "Session: 1234567…" raw slice prefix: "1234567\ud83d" raw slice encodeURIComponent FAILED: URI malformed new label encodeURIComponent ok ``` - **Browser-rendered proof:** The same rendered DOM was loaded in a real browser and produced the visible chip below. target.title: fix(cli): one-shot agent --local runs never export OTel diagnostics
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where one-shot `openclaw agent --local` runs would export no OTel telemetry at all when `diagnostics.otel.enabled: true` and the `diagnostics-otel` plugin are configured: zero spans, metrics, or logs reached the OTLP collector, while the same turns dispatched through the Gateway exported fine. Gateway-to-embedded fallback runs (gateway timeout or transport failure) silently dropped telemetry the same way, so exactly the runs that bypass the Gateway were invisible in tracing backends.

## Why This Change Was Made

Diagnostics exporters are plugin services and were only ever started inside the Gateway process (`startPluginServices` at gateway startup/reload); embedded CLI runs emit diagnostic events in the CLI process where nothing subscribes. The CLI now starts the `diagnostics-otel` service around embedded agent runs via a scoped, non-activating plugin load that honors the same plugin-enablement config as the Gateway, and flushes on exit: drain the async diagnostic-event queue, then shut the SDK down (force flush), bounded by a 10s timeout so an unreachable collector cannot hang the CLI. `diagnostics-prometheus` intentionally stays Gateway-only — it is a pull-based scrape server that is useless in a short-lived process and would race the Gateway for its port. No new config surface; configs without OTel enabled short-circuit before any plugin load.

## User Impact

Operators running one-shot `openclaw agent --local` turns (and runs that fall back from the Gateway to the embedded agent) now get the same OTel traces, metrics, and logs as Gateway-executed turns, flushed before the process exits. Setups without OTel export enabled are unaffected.

## Evidence

- Live before/after on macOS against a local Arize Phoenix OTLP collector: before, one-shot `--local` runs produced zero spans while Gateway runs exported fine; after, a one-shot run logs `diagnostics-otel: logs exporter enabled (OTLP/Protobuf)` and `openclaw.harness.run`, `openclaw.run`, and `openclaw.model.call` spans (with `gen_ai.*` attributes) arrive in Phoenix seconds after the process exits.
